column2: A v2 envelope that binds the scope returns if a bundle proves the acceptance terms were covered by the signature; until then the v1 role rule is the only honest one.
The "separate caller enumerator" idea returns if a schema uses dynamic dispatch (EXECUTE with a computed name) that a static chain cannot follow.
A single-implementation gate returns if an independently written verifier agrees on every mutation of the corpus.
The weaker signature form returns if a relying party accepts it explicitly as provenance-only, in a policy that names it.
Rust core returns if a working linker is available on the target host and the differential can be extended to the level ladder.
The float rule returns if a cross-language canonical form is standardised (RFC 8785bis) and implemented by both Python and JavaScript.
The "artifact improves recall" hypothesis returns with a schema whose bypass is not derivable from the catalogue alone, measured on a non-expert reader.
Same as E-M73: a schema whose bypass is hidden in a combination, plus a reader who cannot reason about Postgres semantics.
The false-pass control returns if a guard starts reading the filesystem instead of `git ls-files`.
